clue.text: German government half affected by the spirit of yesterday?

definitions.text: affected by the spirit of yesterday?

parts.note: Hun is an old, derogatory name for a German

indicators.note: half of the ten-letter word government is taken, its first five letters

explanation.surface: A remark about the German government seemingly being under the sway of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the front half of 'government', GOVER. 'The spirit of yesterday' is a playful definition: the spirits drunk yesterday leave you feeling rough today.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering after last night's drinking feels the effect of yesterday's alcohol, the spirits of yesterday.

clue.text: Revolting hothead with more mature supporter

parts.note: people revolting are up in arms, so up
the head, or first letter, of hot
more mature means older

explanation.surface: A rebellious young firebrand alongside a wiser elder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' gives UP, as in a people being up in arms.
explanation.definitionFit: One who upholds something keeps it up, a backer or defender.

clue.text: Instrument — loosely speaking, not a cello

indicators.note: loosely means the letters are put together in a free, rearranged order
not tells us the letter of the word a is absent from the mixed letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone, loosely speaking, says an instrument isn't a cello.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix SPEAKING with CELLO; 'not a' says one A must be left out, and the remaining twelve letters give the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A glockenspiel is a percussion instrument of tuned metal bars struck with hammers.

clue.text: Character sketch composed as conclusion of positive vetting

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so these letters are rearranged
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A brief portrait of someone written up as the final step of a security check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges VETTING to VIGNETT; 'conclusion of positive' adds E at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a short descriptive piece of writing that portrays a person.

clue.text: Elizabeth's favourite capital city

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was a favourite courtier of Queen Elizabeth I; Raleigh is also the state capital of North Carolina.

clue.text: Surrender document I have written during fighting

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: fighting means war
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A document of surrender being drawn up while the battle still rages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' signals that one piece sits inside the other; 'Surrender document' is the definition, though 'Surrender' could pass for a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiver is a written statement giving up, or surrendering, a right or claim.

clue.text: Open University given new function

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: The Open University is assigned a new role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open University' looks like the name of the institution, but 'Open' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or parcel is to unfasten it.

clue.text: Young male model abducted, by Jove!

definitions.text: Young male model abducted, by Jove!

parts.words: Young male model abducted, by Jove!
parts.note: reads as an exclamation about a kidnapped model, but refers to the beautiful Trojan youth carried off by Jove (Jupiter, Zeus) to be cupbearer to the gods

explanation.surface: A startled exclamation at news of a young male model being kidnapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by Jove!' seems a mild oath, but it is literal: Jove was the abductor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the shepherd boy of Troy was seized by Zeus in eagle form, making him the archetypal handsome youth.

clue.text: Female runner second in race in capital city

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the city name

parts.note: Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: the second letter in the word race is picked

explanation.surface: A woman athlete competing in a race held in a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the A from 'second in race' inside the Georgia capital, not the Greek capital one might first think of.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atalanta was a huntress famed for her speed in a footrace against her suitors.

clue.text: Little chap left when girl abandoned religion

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the girl's name is dropped from the word

parts.note: theosophy is a religious-philosophical movement
Sophy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A small boy stays behind after a girl turns her back on her faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when girl abandoned' strips SOPHY from THEOSOPHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Theo is a pet form of Theodore, so a shortened boy's name.

clue.text: Can roots very rampantly spread here?

definitions.text: Can roots very rampantly spread here?

indicators.note: rampantly means wildly and without restraint, so these letters run riot

explanation.surface: Asking whether plant roots could grow wildly in a glasshouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampantly' rearranges CAN ROOTS VERY; the whole clue also describes a glasshouse where plants flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatory is a glass room where plants are grown, so roots may spread there.

clue.text: Businesses are unable to raise capital for plant

parts.note: trades are lines of business
are unable means can't

indicators.note: raise in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: capital means excellent, A1, with the 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: Firms are unable to raise money for a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money, but means excellent, A1; 'raise' turns it to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradescantia is a genus of trailing houseplants, also called spiderwort.

clue.text: Dear TV broadcast?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread out anew

explanation.surface: A question about an expensive television transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges DEAR TV; television advertising is costly, hence 'Dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial shown on television is a costly broadcast promotion.

clue.text: Girl who's closely related I embraced

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: germane means relevant or closely related

explanation.surface: A girl who is a close relative gets hugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced' puts I inside GERMANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine is a woman's given name, as in Germaine Greer.

clue.text: Italian duke cut flower

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: Prospero is the rightful Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest

explanation.surface: An Italian nobleman snips a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a verb, meaning to flourish, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: To flower in the sense of flourish or thrive.

clue.text: Flower bringing back pain after Pa suffers a loss

indicators.note: after places the word for back pain behind the remaining letter
suffers a loss says a letter a goes missing from the word

parts.note: lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: Dad's bereavement is followed by a bout of back trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing back pain' looks like one phrase, but 'back pain' is LUMBAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago, or leadwort, is a shrub grown for its blue flowers.

clue.text: Transgression concerning criminal

parts.note: concerning means about, of
a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: A wrongdoing relating to a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A FENCE, in criminal slang, deals in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of law or a wrong act.

clue.text: Set up Eastern transport system some time ago

parts.note: to set up something is to form it
Rly is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: An Eastern rail network was established long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: RLY is the standard abbreviation for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly means in the past, previously.

clue.text: Damn swindle uncovered by investigation

parts.note: a con is a swindle
something uncovered by investigation has been found

explanation.surface: Cursing a fraud exposed by an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damn' is an exclamation, as in 'Confound it!'
explanation.definitionFit: Confound is an old oath, used just like damn.

clue.text: Mounted soldiers — they can go on board any time

definitions.text: they can go on board any time

explanation.definitionFit: Medieval cavalrymen in armour; also the chess pieces that move across the board, playable at any point in a game.

clue.text: Not invited to be spontaneous

explanation.definitionFit: Unbidden means uninvited, or arising of its own accord without prompting.

clue.text: Keep on supporting fellow-judge

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting the others sits beneath them

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Continue backing a fellow judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is a noun, the castle stronghold, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A donjon is the great tower or keep of a castle.

clue.text: Late or middle fourteenth century Italian style

indicators.note: middle means only the central part is kept, so the outer letters go

parts.note: the trecento is the 14th century in Italian art and literature

explanation.surface: Describing an artistic style of the Italian 1300s.
explanation.walkthrough: TRECENTO is the 1300s in Italian art; 'middle' keeps all but its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent and late both mean having happened not long ago, as in the late news.

clue.text: Cash on delivery for sporting facility

indicators.note: on in an across clue places one piece after another

parts.note: in cricket a delivery is the act of bowling
green is slang for money

explanation.surface: Paying cash on delivery for a sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cash on delivery' looks like the shipping term; 'on' in an across clue puts the money word after the cricket word. A bowling green is a lawn for playing bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowling green is a smooth lawn on which the game of bowls is played.

clue.text: Prosperity raised as a result of strike

definitions.text: raised as a result of strike

explanation.definitionFit: Weal means well-being or prosperity, as in commonweal; it is also a raised mark on the skin left by a blow.

clue.text: Soundly educated, fully stretched

indicators.note: soundly tells us the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: educated means taught

explanation.surface: Someone well schooled and thoroughly extended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like it means thoroughly, but it signals a word heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope pulled tight with no slack is fully stretched.

clue.text: End picket? That might deflect striker's effort

explanation.definitionFit: Each upright at either end of a pitch is a kind of stake, and a shot from a forward can hit the woodwork and rebound.

clue.text: How those rising took flight and defeated prince, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Bonnie Prince Charlie, beaten at Culloden, fled towards the Isle of Skye

explanation.surface: How the beaten prince fled, and how climbers ascend.
explanation.walkthrough: After Culloden (1746) Bonnie Prince Charlie escaped 'over the sea to Skye', heading Skye-wards.
explanation.definitionFit: Things rising and flying off go up towards the heavens.
